[748](https://docs.rs#748)    /// Return an *iterable* that can chunk the iterator.
[749](https://docs.rs#749)    ///
[750](https://docs.rs#750)    /// Yield subiterators (chunks) that each yield a fixed number elements,
[751](https://docs.rs#751)    /// determined by `size`. The last chunk will be shorter if there aren't
[752](https://docs.rs#752)    /// enough elements.
[753](https://docs.rs#753)    ///
[754](https://docs.rs#754)    /// `IntoChunks` is based on `ChunkBy`: it is iterable (implements
[755](https://docs.rs#755)    /// `IntoIterator`, **not** `Iterator`), and it only buffers if several
[756](https://docs.rs#756)    /// chunk iterators are alive at the same time.
[757](https://docs.rs#757)    ///
[758](https://docs.rs#758)    /// Iterator element type is `Chunk`, each chunk's iterator.
[759](https://docs.rs#759)    ///
[760](https://docs.rs#760)    /// **Panics** if `size` is 0.
[761](https://docs.rs#761)    ///
[762](https://docs.rs#762)    /// # Examples
[763](https://docs.rs#763)    ///
[764](https://docs.rs#764)    /// ```
[765](https://docs.rs#765)    /// use itertools::Itertools;
[766](https://docs.rs#766)    ///
[767](https://docs.rs#767)    /// let data = vec![1, 1, 2, -2, 6, 0, 3, 1];
[768](https://docs.rs#768)    /// //chunk size=3 |------->|-------->|--->|
[769](https://docs.rs#769)    ///
[770](https://docs.rs#770)    /// // Note: The `&` is significant here, `IntoChunks` is iterable
[771](https://docs.rs#771)    /// // only by reference. You can also call `.into_iter()` explicitly.
[772](https://docs.rs#772)    /// for chunk in &data.into_iter().chunks(3) {
[773](https://docs.rs#773)    ///     // Check that the sum of each chunk is 4.
[774](https://docs.rs#774)    ///     assert_eq!(4, chunk.sum());
[775](https://docs.rs#775)    /// }
[776](https://docs.rs#776)    /// ```
[777](https://docs.rs#777)    ///
[778](https://docs.rs#778)    /// ```should_panic
[779](https://docs.rs#779)    /// use itertools::Itertools;
[780](https://docs.rs#780)    /// let data = vec![1, 2, 3];
[781](https://docs.rs#781)    /// // Panics because chunk size is 0.
[782](https://docs.rs#782)    /// let _chunks = data.into_iter().chunks(0);
[783](https://docs.rs#783)    /// ```
[784](https://docs.rs#784)    #[cfg(feature = "use_alloc")]
[785](https://docs.rs#785)    fn chunks(self, size: usize) -> IntoChunks<Self>
[786](https://docs.rs#786)    where
[787](https://docs.rs#787)        Self: Sized,
[788](https://docs.rs#788)    {
[789](https://docs.rs#789)        assert!(size != 0);
[790](https://docs.rs#790)        groupbylazy::new_chunks(self, size)
[791](https://docs.rs#791)    }
[792](https://docs.rs#792)
[793](https://docs.rs#793)    /// Return an iterator over all contiguous windows producing tuples of
[794](https://docs.rs#794)    /// a specific size (up to 12).
[795](https://docs.rs#795)    ///
[796](https://docs.rs#796)    /// `tuple_windows` clones the iterator elements so that they can be
[797](https://docs.rs#797)    /// part of successive windows, this makes it most suited for iterators
[798](https://docs.rs#798)    /// of references and other values that are cheap to copy.
[799](https://docs.rs#799)    ///
[800](https://docs.rs#800)    /// ```
[801](https://docs.rs#801)    /// use itertools::Itertools;
[802](https://docs.rs#802)    /// let mut v = Vec::new();
[803](https://docs.rs#803)    ///
[804](https://docs.rs#804)    /// // pairwise iteration
[805](https://docs.rs#805)    /// for (a, b) in (1..5).tuple_windows() {
[806](https://docs.rs#806)    ///     v.push((a, b));
[807](https://docs.rs#807)    /// }
[808](https://docs.rs#808)    /// assert_eq!(v, vec![(1, 2), (2, 3), (3, 4)]);
[809](https://docs.rs#809)    ///
[810](https://docs.rs#810)    /// let mut it = (1..5).tuple_windows();
[811](https://docs.rs#811)    /// assert_eq!(Some((1, 2, 3)), it.next());
[812](https://docs.rs#812)    /// assert_eq!(Some((2, 3, 4)), it.next());
[813](https://docs.rs#813)    /// assert_eq!(None, it.next());
[814](https://docs.rs#814)    ///
[815](https://docs.rs#815)    /// // this requires a type hint
[816](https://docs.rs#816)    /// let it = (1..5).tuple_windows::<(_, _, _)>();
[817](https://docs.rs#817)    /// itertools::assert_equal(it, vec![(1, 2, 3), (2, 3, 4)]);
[818](https://docs.rs#818)    ///
[819](https://docs.rs#819)    /// // you can also specify the complete type
[820](https://docs.rs#820)    /// use itertools::TupleWindows;
[821](https://docs.rs#821)    /// use std::ops::Range;
[822](https://docs.rs#822)    ///
[823](https://docs.rs#823)    /// let it: TupleWindows<Range<u32>, (u32, u32, u32)> = (1..5).tuple_windows();
[824](https://docs.rs#824)    /// itertools::assert_equal(it, vec![(1, 2, 3), (2, 3, 4)]);
[825](https://docs.rs#825)    /// ```
[826](https://docs.rs#826)    fn tuple_windows<T>(self) -> TupleWindows<Self, T>
[827](https://docs.rs#827)    where
[828](https://docs.rs#828)        Self: Sized + Iterator<Item = T::Item>,
[829](https://docs.rs#829)        T: traits::HomogeneousTuple,
[830](https://docs.rs#830)        T::Item: Clone,
[831](https://docs.rs#831)    {
[832](https://docs.rs#832)        tuple_impl::tuple_windows(self)
[833](https://docs.rs#833)    }

[835](https://docs.rs#835)    /// Return an iterator over all windows, wrapping back to the first
[836](https://docs.rs#836)    /// elements when the window would otherwise exceed the length of the
[837](https://docs.rs#837)    /// iterator, producing tuples of a specific size (up to 12).
[838](https://docs.rs#838)    ///
[839](https://docs.rs#839)    /// `circular_tuple_windows` clones the iterator elements so that they can be
[840](https://docs.rs#840)    /// part of successive windows, this makes it most suited for iterators
[841](https://docs.rs#841)    /// of references and other values that are cheap to copy.
[842](https://docs.rs#842)    ///
[843](https://docs.rs#843)    /// ```
[844](https://docs.rs#844)    /// use itertools::Itertools;
[845](https://docs.rs#845)    /// let mut v = Vec::new();
[846](https://docs.rs#846)    /// for (a, b) in (1..5).circular_tuple_windows() {
[847](https://docs.rs#847)    ///     v.push((a, b));
[848](https://docs.rs#848)    /// }
[849](https://docs.rs#849)    /// assert_eq!(v, vec![(1, 2), (2, 3), (3, 4), (4, 1)]);
[850](https://docs.rs#850)    ///
[851](https://docs.rs#851)    /// let mut it = (1..5).circular_tuple_windows();
[852](https://docs.rs#852)    /// assert_eq!(Some((1, 2, 3)), it.next());
[853](https://docs.rs#853)    /// assert_eq!(Some((2, 3, 4)), it.next());
[854](https://docs.rs#854)    /// assert_eq!(Some((3, 4, 1)), it.next());
[855](https://docs.rs#855)    /// assert_eq!(Some((4, 1, 2)), it.next());
[856](https://docs.rs#856)    /// assert_eq!(None, it.next());
[857](https://docs.rs#857)    ///
[858](https://docs.rs#858)    /// // this requires a type hint
[859](https://docs.rs#859)    /// let it = (1..5).circular_tuple_windows::<(_, _, _)>();
[860](https://docs.rs#860)    /// itertools::assert_equal(it, vec![(1, 2, 3), (2, 3, 4), (3, 4, 1), (4, 1, 2)]);
[861](https://docs.rs#861)    /// ```
[862](https://docs.rs#862)    fn circular_tuple_windows<T>(self) -> CircularTupleWindows<Self, T>
[863](https://docs.rs#863)    where
[864](https://docs.rs#864)        Self: Sized + Clone + Iterator<Item = T::Item> + ExactSizeIterator,
[865](https://docs.rs#865)        T: tuple_impl::TupleCollect + Clone,
[866](https://docs.rs#866)        T::Item: Clone,
[867](https://docs.rs#867)    {
[868](https://docs.rs#868)        tuple_impl::circular_tuple_windows(self)
[869](https://docs.rs#869)    }
[870](https://docs.rs#870)    /// Return an iterator that groups the items in tuples of a specific size
[871](https://docs.rs#871)    /// (up to 12).
[872](https://docs.rs#872)    ///
[873](https://docs.rs#873)    /// See also the method [`.next_tuple()`](Itertools::next_tuple).
[874](https://docs.rs#874)    ///
[875](https://docs.rs#875)    /// ```
[876](https://docs.rs#876)    /// use itertools::Itertools;
[877](https://docs.rs#877)    /// let mut v = Vec::new();
[878](https://docs.rs#878)    /// for (a, b) in (1..5).tuples() {

[884](https://docs.rs#884)    /// assert_eq!(Some((1, 2, 3)), it.next());
[885](https://docs.rs#885)    /// assert_eq!(Some((4, 5, 6)), it.next());
[886](https://docs.rs#886)    /// assert_eq!(None, it.next());
[887](https://docs.rs#887)    ///
[888](https://docs.rs#888)    /// // this requires a type hint
[889](https://docs.rs#889)    /// let it = (1..7).tuples::<(_, _, _)>();
[890](https://docs.rs#890)    /// itertools::assert_equal(it, vec![(1, 2, 3), (4, 5, 6)]);
[891](https://docs.rs#891)    ///
[892](https://docs.rs#892)    /// // you can also specify the complete type
[893](https://docs.rs#893)    /// use itertools::Tuples;
[894](https://docs.rs#894)    /// use std::ops::Range;
[895](https://docs.rs#895)    ///
[896](https://docs.rs#896)    /// let it: Tuples<Range<u32>, (u32, u32, u32)> = (1..7).tuples();
[897](https://docs.rs#897)    /// itertools::assert_equal(it, vec![(1, 2, 3), (4, 5, 6)]);
[898](https://docs.rs#898)    /// ```
[899](https://docs.rs#899)    ///
[900](https://docs.rs#900)    /// See also [`Tuples::into_buffer`].
[901](https://docs.rs#901)    fn tuples<T>(self) -> Tuples<Self, T>
[902](https://docs.rs#902)    where
[903](https://docs.rs#903)        Self: Sized + Iterator<Item = T::Item>,
[904](https://docs.rs#904)        T: traits::HomogeneousTuple,

[908](https://docs.rs#908)
[909](https://docs.rs#909)    /// Return an iterator over all contiguous windows, producing
[910](https://docs.rs#910)    /// arrays of size `N`.
[911](https://docs.rs#911)    ///
[912](https://docs.rs#912)    /// `array_windows` clones the iterator elements so that they can be
[913](https://docs.rs#913)    /// part of successive windows. This makes it most suited for iterators
[914](https://docs.rs#914)    /// of references and other values that are cheap to copy.
[915](https://docs.rs#915)    ///
[916](https://docs.rs#916)    /// If the input iterator contains fewer than `N` items, no
[917](https://docs.rs#917)    /// windows are returned. Otherwise, if the input iterator
[918](https://docs.rs#918)    /// contains `k` items, exactly `k+N-1` windows are returned.
[919](https://docs.rs#919)    ///
[920](https://docs.rs#920)    /// (This formula still applies when `N==0`, and means that `k+1`
[921](https://docs.rs#921)    /// zero-length windows are returned for `k` input items.)
[922](https://docs.rs#922)    ///
[923](https://docs.rs#923)    /// ```
[924](https://docs.rs#924)    /// use itertools::Itertools;
[925](https://docs.rs#925)    ///
[926](https://docs.rs#926)    /// // Three-element windows from the items [1, 2, 3, 4, 5].
[927](https://docs.rs#927)    /// itertools::assert_equal(
[928](https://docs.rs#928)    ///     (1..6).array_windows::<3>(),
[929](https://docs.rs#929)    ///     vec![[1, 2, 3], [2, 3, 4], [3, 4, 5]]
[930](https://docs.rs#930)    /// );
[931](https://docs.rs#931)    ///
[932](https://docs.rs#932)    /// // When the input list is shorter than the window size, no windows
[933](https://docs.rs#933)    /// // are returned at all.
[934](https://docs.rs#934)    /// let mut windows = (1..6).array_windows::<10>();
[935](https://docs.rs#935)    /// assert_eq!(None, windows.next());
[936](https://docs.rs#936)    ///
[937](https://docs.rs#937)    /// // When the window size is zero, one more window is returned
[938](https://docs.rs#938)    /// // than there are items.
[939](https://docs.rs#939)    /// itertools::assert_equal((1..6).array_windows::<0>(), vec![[]; 6]);
[940](https://docs.rs#940)    ///
[941](https://docs.rs#941)    /// // In some cases you don't have to specify the window size
[942](https://docs.rs#942)    /// // explicitly with a type hint, because Rust can infer it
[943](https://docs.rs#943)    /// for [a, b, c] in (1..6).array_windows() {
[944](https://docs.rs#944)    ///     println!("{a} {b} {c}");
[945](https://docs.rs#945)    /// }
[946](https://docs.rs#946)    /// ```
[947](https://docs.rs#947)    fn array_windows<const N: usize>(self) -> ArrayWindows<Self, N>
[948](https://docs.rs#948)    where
[949](https://docs.rs#949)        Self: Sized,
[950](https://docs.rs#950)        Self::Item: Clone,
[951](https://docs.rs#951)    {
[952](https://docs.rs#952)        array_impl::array_windows(self)
[953](https://docs.rs#953)    }
[954](https://docs.rs#954)
[955](https://docs.rs#955)    /// Return an iterator over all windows, wrapping back to the first
[956](https://docs.rs#956)    /// elements when the window would otherwise exceed the length of the
[957](https://docs.rs#957)    /// iterator, producing arrays of size `N`.
[958](https://docs.rs#958)    ///
[959](https://docs.rs#959)    /// `circular_array_windows` clones the iterator elements so that
[960](https://docs.rs#960)    /// they can be part of successive windows, this makes it most
[961](https://docs.rs#961)    /// suited for iterators of references and other values that are
[962](https://docs.rs#962)    /// cheap to copy.
[963](https://docs.rs#963)    ///
[964](https://docs.rs#964)    /// One window is returned per element of the input iterator. This
[965](https://docs.rs#965)    /// is true even if the input contains fewer elements than the
[966](https://docs.rs#966)    /// window size. In that situation, input elements are repeated
[967](https://docs.rs#967)    /// within each window. The results are as if the input had been
[968](https://docs.rs#968)    /// treated as a cyclic list, and a window of `N` items had been
[969](https://docs.rs#969)    /// returned for every starting point in the cycle.
[970](https://docs.rs#970)    ///
[971](https://docs.rs#971)    /// (If the window size is zero, the function _still_ returns one
[972](https://docs.rs#972)    /// empty window per element of the input iterator.)
[973](https://docs.rs#973)    ///
[974](https://docs.rs#974)    /// ```
[975](https://docs.rs#975)    /// use itertools::Itertools;
[976](https://docs.rs#976)    ///
[977](https://docs.rs#977)    /// // Three-element windows from [1, 2, 3, 4, 5], with two of
[978](https://docs.rs#978)    /// // them wrapping round from 5 to 1.
[979](https://docs.rs#979)    /// itertools::assert_equal(
[980](https://docs.rs#980)    ///     (1..6).circular_array_windows::<3>(),
[981](https://docs.rs#981)    ///     vec![[1, 2, 3], [2, 3, 4], [3, 4, 5], [4, 5, 1], [5, 1, 2]]
[982](https://docs.rs#982)    /// );
[983](https://docs.rs#983)    ///
[984](https://docs.rs#984)    /// // If the input is shorter than the window size, input
[985](https://docs.rs#985)    /// // items are repeated even within the same window.
[986](https://docs.rs#986)    /// itertools::assert_equal(
[987](https://docs.rs#987)    ///     (1..3).circular_array_windows::<5>(),
[988](https://docs.rs#988)    ///     vec![[1, 2, 1, 2, 1], [2, 1, 2, 1, 2]]
[989](https://docs.rs#989)    /// );
[990](https://docs.rs#990)    ///
[991](https://docs.rs#991)    /// // If the input contains only one item, the returned window
[992](https://docs.rs#992)    /// // repeats it N times.
[993](https://docs.rs#993)    /// let once = std::iter::once(1);
[994](https://docs.rs#994)    /// itertools::assert_equal(
[995](https://docs.rs#995)    ///     once.circular_array_windows::<3>(),
[996](https://docs.rs#996)    ///     vec![[1, 1, 1]]
[997](https://docs.rs#997)    /// );
[998](https://docs.rs#998)    ///
[999](https://docs.rs#999)    /// // If the input is empty, no windows are returned at all.
[1000](https://docs.rs#1000)    /// let empty = std::iter::empty::<i32>();
[1001](https://docs.rs#1001)    /// let mut windows = empty.circular_array_windows::<5>();
[1002](https://docs.rs#1002)    /// assert_eq!(None, windows.next());
[1003](https://docs.rs#1003)    ///
[1004](https://docs.rs#1004)    /// // If the input is empty, no windows are returned at all.
[1005](https://docs.rs#1005)    /// let empty = std::iter::empty::<i32>();
[1006](https://docs.rs#1006)    /// let mut windows = empty.circular_array_windows::<5>();
[1007](https://docs.rs#1007)    /// assert_eq!(None, windows.next());
[1008](https://docs.rs#1008)    ///
[1009](https://docs.rs#1009)    /// // One window is returned per item, even if the windows are empty.
[1010](https://docs.rs#1010)    /// itertools::assert_equal(
[1011](https://docs.rs#1011)    ///     (1..6).circular_array_windows::<0>(),
[1012](https://docs.rs#1012)    ///     vec![[]; 5]
[1013](https://docs.rs#1013)    /// );
[1014](https://docs.rs#1014)    ///
[1015](https://docs.rs#1015)    /// // In some cases you don't have to specify the window size
[1016](https://docs.rs#1016)    /// // explicitly with a type hint, because Rust can infer it.
[1017](https://docs.rs#1017)    /// for [a, b, c] in (1..10).circular_array_windows() {
[1018](https://docs.rs#1018)    ///     println!("{a} {b} {c}");
[1019](https://docs.rs#1019)    /// }
[1020](https://docs.rs#1020)    /// ```
[1021](https://docs.rs#1021)    fn circular_array_windows<const N: usize>(self) -> CircularArrayWindows<Self, N>
[1022](https://docs.rs#1022)    where
[1023](https://docs.rs#1023)        Self: Sized,
[1024](https://docs.rs#1024)        Self::Item: Clone,
[1025](https://docs.rs#1025)    {
[1026](https://docs.rs#1026)        array_impl::circular_array_windows(self)
[1027](https://docs.rs#1027)    }
[1028](https://docs.rs#1028)
[1029](https://docs.rs#1029)    /// Split into an iterator pair that both yield all elements from
[1030](https://docs.rs#1030)    /// the original iterator.
[1031](https://docs.rs#1031)    ///
[1032](https://docs.rs#1032)    /// **Note:** If the iterator is cloneable, prefer using that instead
[1033](https://docs.rs#1033)    /// of using this method. Cloning is likely to be more efficient.

[1041](https://docs.rs#1041)    /// let (mut t1, t2) = xs.into_iter().tee();

[1045](https://docs.rs#1045)    /// ```
[1046](https://docs.rs#1046)    #[cfg(feature = "use_alloc")]
[1047](https://docs.rs#1047)    fn tee(self) -> (Tee<Self>, Tee<Self>)
[1048](https://docs.rs#1048)    where
[1049](https://docs.rs#1049)        Self: Sized,
[1050](https://docs.rs#1050)        Self::Item: Clone,
[1051](https://docs.rs#1051)    {

[1053](https://docs.rs#1053)    }

[1129](https://docs.rs#1129)
[1130](https://docs.rs#1130)    /// Return an iterator adaptor that flattens every `Result::Ok` value into
[1131](https://docs.rs#1131)    /// a series of `Result::Ok` values. `Result::Err` values are unchanged.
[1132](https://docs.rs#1132)    ///
[1133](https://docs.rs#1133)    /// This is useful when you have some common error type for your crate and
[1134](https://docs.rs#1134)    /// need to propagate it upwards, but the `Result::Ok` case needs to be flattened.
[1135](https://docs.rs#1135)    ///
[1136](https://docs.rs#1136)    /// ```
[1137](https://docs.rs#1137)    /// use itertools::Itertools;
[1138](https://docs.rs#1138)    ///
[1139](https://docs.rs#1139)    /// let input = vec![Ok(0..2), Err(false), Ok(2..4)];
[1140](https://docs.rs#1140)    /// let it = input.iter().cloned().flatten_ok();
[1141](https://docs.rs#1141)    /// itertools::assert_equal(it.clone(), vec![Ok(0), Ok(1), Err(false), Ok(2), Ok(3)]);
[1142](https://docs.rs#1142)    ///
[1143](https://docs.rs#1143)    /// // This can also be used to propagate errors when collecting.
[1144](https://docs.rs#1144)    /// let output_result: Result<Vec<i32>, bool> = it.collect();
[1145](https://docs.rs#1145)    /// assert_eq!(output_result, Err(false));
[1146](https://docs.rs#1146)    /// ```
[1147](https://docs.rs#1147)    fn flatten_ok<T, E>(self) -> FlattenOk<Self, T, E>
[1148](https://docs.rs#1148)    where
[1149](https://docs.rs#1149)        Self: Iterator<Item = Result<T, E>> + Sized,
[1150](https://docs.rs#1150)        T: IntoIterator,
[1151](https://docs.rs#1151)    {
[1152](https://docs.rs#1152)        flatten_ok::flatten_ok(self)
[1153](https://docs.rs#1153)    }

[1155](https://docs.rs#1155)    /// “Lift” a function of the values of the current iterator so as to process
[1156](https://docs.rs#1156)    /// an iterator of `Result` values instead.
[1157](https://docs.rs#1157)    ///
[1158](https://docs.rs#1158)    /// `processor` is a closure that receives an adapted version of the iterator
[1159](https://docs.rs#1159)    /// as the only argument — the adapted iterator produces elements of type `T`,
[1160](https://docs.rs#1160)    /// as long as the original iterator produces `Ok` values.
[1161](https://docs.rs#1161)    ///
[1162](https://docs.rs#1162)    /// If the original iterable produces an error at any point, the adapted
[1163](https://docs.rs#1163)    /// iterator ends and it will return the error itself.
[1164](https://docs.rs#1164)    ///
[1165](https://docs.rs#1165)    /// Otherwise, the return value from the closure is returned wrapped
[1166](https://docs.rs#1166)    /// inside `Ok`.
[1167](https://docs.rs#1167)    ///
[1168](https://docs.rs#1168)    /// # Example
[1169](https://docs.rs#1169)    ///
[1170](https://docs.rs#1170)    /// ```
[1171](https://docs.rs#1171)    /// use itertools::Itertools;
[1172](https://docs.rs#1172)    ///
[1173](https://docs.rs#1173)    /// type Item = Result<i32, &'static str>;
[1174](https://docs.rs#1174)    ///
[1175](https://docs.rs#1175)    /// let first_values: Vec<Item> = vec![Ok(1), Ok(0), Ok(3)];
[1176](https://docs.rs#1176)    /// let second_values: Vec<Item> = vec![Ok(2), Ok(1), Err("overflow")];
[1177](https://docs.rs#1177)    ///
[1178](https://docs.rs#1178)    /// // “Lift” the iterator .max() method to work on the Ok-values.
[1179](https://docs.rs#1179)    /// let first_max = first_values.into_iter().process_results(|iter| iter.max().unwrap_or(0));
[1180](https://docs.rs#1180)    /// let second_max = second_values.into_iter().process_results(|iter| iter.max().unwrap_or(0));
[1181](https://docs.rs#1181)    ///
[1182](https://docs.rs#1182)    /// assert_eq!(first_max, Ok(3));
[1183](https://docs.rs#1183)    /// assert!(second_max.is_err());
[1184](https://docs.rs#1184)    /// ```
[1185](https://docs.rs#1185)    fn process_results<F, T, E, R>(self, processor: F) -> Result<R, E>
[1186](https://docs.rs#1186)    where
[1187](https://docs.rs#1187)        Self: Iterator<Item = Result<T, E>> + Sized,
[1188](https://docs.rs#1188)        F: FnOnce(ProcessResults<Self, E>) -> R,
[1189](https://docs.rs#1189)    {
[1190](https://docs.rs#1190)        process_results(self, processor)
[1191](https://docs.rs#1191)    }
[1192](https://docs.rs#1192)

[1216](https://docs.rs#1216)    /// Return an iterator adaptor that merges the two base iterators in order.

[1226](https://docs.rs#1226)    /// let a = (0..).zip("bc".chars());

[1230](https://docs.rs#1230)    /// ```

[1233](https://docs.rs#1233)        Self: Sized,
[1234](https://docs.rs#1234)        J: IntoIterator<Item = Self::Item>,

[1239](https://docs.rs#1239)
[1240](https://docs.rs#1240)    /// Create an iterator that merges items from both this and the specified
[1241](https://docs.rs#1241)    /// iterator in ascending order.
[1242](https://docs.rs#1242)    ///
[1243](https://docs.rs#1243)    /// The function can either return an `Ordering` variant or a boolean.
[1244](https://docs.rs#1244)    ///
[1245](https://docs.rs#1245)    /// If `cmp_fn` returns `Ordering`,
[1246](https://docs.rs#1246)    /// it chooses whether to pair elements based on the `Ordering` returned by the
[1247](https://docs.rs#1247)    /// specified compare function. At any point, inspecting the tip of the
[1248](https://docs.rs#1248)    /// iterators `I` and `J` as items `i` of type `I::Item` and `j` of type
[1249](https://docs.rs#1249)    /// `J::Item` respectively, the resulting iterator will:
[1250](https://docs.rs#1250)    ///
[1251](https://docs.rs#1251)    /// - Emit `EitherOrBoth::Left(i)` when `i < j`,
[1252](https://docs.rs#1252)    ///   and remove `i` from its source iterator
[1253](https://docs.rs#1253)    /// - Emit `EitherOrBoth::Right(j)` when `i > j`,
[1254](https://docs.rs#1254)    ///   and remove `j` from its source iterator
[1255](https://docs.rs#1255)    /// - Emit `EitherOrBoth::Both(i, j)` when  `i == j`,
[1256](https://docs.rs#1256)    ///   and remove both `i` and `j` from their respective source iterators
[1257](https://docs.rs#1257)    ///
[1258](https://docs.rs#1258)    /// ```
[1259](https://docs.rs#1259)    /// use itertools::EitherOrBoth::{Both, Left, Right};
[1260](https://docs.rs#1260)    /// use itertools::Itertools;
[1261](https://docs.rs#1261)    ///
[1262](https://docs.rs#1262)    /// let a = vec![0, 2, 4, 6, 1].into_iter();
[1263](https://docs.rs#1263)    /// let b = (0..10).step_by(3);
[1264](https://docs.rs#1264)    ///
[1265](https://docs.rs#1265)    /// itertools::assert_equal(
[1266](https://docs.rs#1266)    ///     // This performs a diff in the style of the Unix command comm(1),
[1267](https://docs.rs#1267)    ///     // generalized to arbitrary types rather than text.
[1268](https://docs.rs#1268)    ///     a.merge_join_by(b, Ord::cmp),
[1269](https://docs.rs#1269)    ///     vec![Both(0, 0), Left(2), Right(3), Left(4), Both(6, 6), Left(1), Right(9)]
[1270](https://docs.rs#1270)    /// );
[1271](https://docs.rs#1271)    /// ```
[1272](https://docs.rs#1272)    ///
[1273](https://docs.rs#1273)    /// If `cmp_fn` returns `bool`,
[1274](https://docs.rs#1274)    /// it chooses whether to pair elements based on the boolean returned by the
[1275](https://docs.rs#1275)    /// specified function. At any point, inspecting the tip of the
[1276](https://docs.rs#1276)    /// iterators `I` and `J` as items `i` of type `I::Item` and `j` of type
[1277](https://docs.rs#1277)    /// `J::Item` respectively, the resulting iterator will:
[1278](https://docs.rs#1278)    ///
[1279](https://docs.rs#1279)    /// - Emit `Either::Left(i)` when `true`,
[1280](https://docs.rs#1280)    ///   and remove `i` from its source iterator
[1281](https://docs.rs#1281)    /// - Emit `Either::Right(j)` when `false`,
[1282](https://docs.rs#1282)    ///   and remove `j` from its source iterator
[1283](https://docs.rs#1283)    ///
[1284](https://docs.rs#1284)    /// It is similar to the `Ordering` case if the first argument is considered
[1285](https://docs.rs#1285)    /// "less" than the second argument.
[1286](https://docs.rs#1286)    ///
[1287](https://docs.rs#1287)    /// ```
[1288](https://docs.rs#1288)    /// use itertools::Either::{Left, Right};
[1289](https://docs.rs#1289)    /// use itertools::Itertools;
[1290](https://docs.rs#1290)    ///
[1291](https://docs.rs#1291)    /// let a = vec![0, 2, 4, 6, 1].into_iter();
[1292](https://docs.rs#1292)    /// let b = (0..10).step_by(3);
[1293](https://docs.rs#1293)    ///
[1294](https://docs.rs#1294)    /// itertools::assert_equal(
[1295](https://docs.rs#1295)    ///     a.merge_join_by(b, |i, j| i <= j),
[1296](https://docs.rs#1296)    ///     vec![Left(0), Right(0), Left(2), Right(3), Left(4), Left(6), Left(1), Right(6), Right(9)]
[1297](https://docs.rs#1297)    /// );
[1298](https://docs.rs#1298)    /// ```
[1299](https://docs.rs#1299)    #[inline]
[1300](https://docs.rs#1300)    #[doc(alias = "comm")]
[1301](https://docs.rs#1301)    fn merge_join_by<J, F, T>(self, other: J, cmp_fn: F) -> MergeJoinBy<Self, J::IntoIter, F>
[1302](https://docs.rs#1302)    where
[1303](https://docs.rs#1303)        J: IntoIterator,
[1304](https://docs.rs#1304)        F: FnMut(&Self::Item, &J::Item) -> T,
[1305](https://docs.rs#1305)        Self: Sized,
[1306](https://docs.rs#1306)    {
[1307](https://docs.rs#1307)        merge_join_by(self, other, cmp_fn)
[1308](https://docs.rs#1308)    }

[1388](https://docs.rs#1388)    /// Return an iterator adaptor that iterates over the cartesian product of
[1389](https://docs.rs#1389)    /// all subiterators returned by meta-iterator `self`.
[1390](https://docs.rs#1390)    ///
[1391](https://docs.rs#1391)    /// All provided iterators must yield the same `Item` type. To generate
[1392](https://docs.rs#1392)    /// the product of iterators yielding multiple types, use the
[1393](https://docs.rs#1393)    /// [`iproduct`] macro instead.
[1394](https://docs.rs#1394)    ///
[1395](https://docs.rs#1395)    /// The iterator element type is `Vec<T>`, where `T` is the iterator element

[1398](https://docs.rs#1398)    /// Note that the iterator is fused.
[1399](https://docs.rs#1399)    ///
[1400](https://docs.rs#1400)    /// ```
[1401](https://docs.rs#1401)    /// use itertools::Itertools;
[1402](https://docs.rs#1402)    /// let mut multi_prod = (0..3).map(|i| (i * 2)..(i * 2 + 2))
[1403](https://docs.rs#1403)    ///     .multi_cartesian_product();
[1404](https://docs.rs#1404)    /// assert_eq!(multi_prod.next(), Some(vec![0, 2, 4]));
[1405](https://docs.rs#1405)    /// assert_eq!(multi_prod.next(), Some(vec![0, 2, 5]));
[1406](https://docs.rs#1406)    /// assert_eq!(multi_prod.next(), Some(vec![0, 3, 4]));
[1407](https://docs.rs#1407)    /// assert_eq!(multi_prod.next(), Some(vec![0, 3, 5]));
[1408](https://docs.rs#1408)    /// assert_eq!(multi_prod.next(), Some(vec![1, 2, 4]));
[1409](https://docs.rs#1409)    /// assert_eq!(multi_prod.next(), Some(vec![1, 2, 5]));
[1410](https://docs.rs#1410)    /// assert_eq!(multi_prod.next(), Some(vec![1, 3, 4]));
[1411](https://docs.rs#1411)    /// assert_eq!(multi_prod.next(), Some(vec![1, 3, 5]));
[1412](https://docs.rs#1412)    /// assert_eq!(multi_prod.next(), None);
[1413](https://docs.rs#1413)    /// ```
[1414](https://docs.rs#1414)    ///
[1415](https://docs.rs#1415)    /// If the adapted iterator is empty, the result is an iterator yielding a single empty vector.
[1416](https://docs.rs#1416)    /// This is known as the [nullary cartesian product](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empty_product#Nullary_Cartesian_product).
[1417](https://docs.rs#1417)    ///
[1418](https://docs.rs#1418)    /// ```
[1419](https://docs.rs#1419)    /// use itertools::Itertools;
[1420](https://docs.rs#1420)    /// let mut nullary_cartesian_product = (0..0).map(|i| (i * 2)..(i * 2 + 2)).multi_cartesian_product();
[1421](https://docs.rs#1421)    /// assert_eq!(nullary_cartesian_product.next(), Some(vec![]));
[1422](https://docs.rs#1422)    /// assert_eq!(nullary_cartesian_product.next(), None);
[1423](https://docs.rs#1423)    /// ```
[1424](https://docs.rs#1424)    #[cfg(feature = "use_alloc")]
[1425](https://docs.rs#1425)    fn multi_cartesian_product(self) -> MultiProduct<<Self::Item as IntoIterator>::IntoIter>

[1427](https://docs.rs#1427)        Self: Sized,

[1430](https://docs.rs#1430)        <Self::Item as IntoIterator>::Item: Clone,

[1435](https://docs.rs#1435)    /// Return an iterator adaptor that uses the passed-in closure to
[1436](https://docs.rs#1436)    /// optionally merge together consecutive elements.
[1437](https://docs.rs#1437)    ///
[1438](https://docs.rs#1438)    /// The closure `f` is passed two elements, `previous` and `current` and may
[1439](https://docs.rs#1439)    /// return either (1) `Ok(combined)` to merge the two values or
[1440](https://docs.rs#1440)    /// (2) `Err((previous', current'))` to indicate they can't be merged.
[1441](https://docs.rs#1441)    /// In (2), the value `previous'` is emitted by the iterator.
[1442](https://docs.rs#1442)    /// Either (1) `combined` or (2) `current'` becomes the previous value
[1443](https://docs.rs#1443)    /// when coalesce continues with the next pair of elements to merge. The
[1444](https://docs.rs#1444)    /// value that remains at the end is also emitted by the iterator.
[1445](https://docs.rs#1445)    ///
[1446](https://docs.rs#1446)    /// Iterator element type is `Self::Item`.
[1447](https://docs.rs#1447)    ///
[1448](https://docs.rs#1448)    /// This iterator is *fused*.
[1449](https://docs.rs#1449)    ///
[1450](https://docs.rs#1450)    /// ```
[1451](https://docs.rs#1451)    /// use itertools::Itertools;
[1452](https://docs.rs#1452)    ///
[1453](https://docs.rs#1453)    /// // sum same-sign runs together
[1454](https://docs.rs#1454)    /// let data = vec![-1., -2., -3., 3., 1., 0., -1.];
[1455](https://docs.rs#1455)    /// itertools::assert_equal(data.into_iter().coalesce(|x, y|
[1456](https://docs.rs#1456)    ///         if (x >= 0.) == (y >= 0.) {
[1457](https://docs.rs#1457)    ///             Ok(x + y)
[1458](https://docs.rs#1458)    ///         } else {
[1459](https://docs.rs#1459)    ///             Err((x, y))
[1460](https://docs.rs#1460)    ///         }),
[1461](https://docs.rs#1461)    ///         vec![-6., 4., -1.]);
[1462](https://docs.rs#1462)    /// ```
[1463](https://docs.rs#1463)    fn coalesce<F>(self, f: F) -> Coalesce<Self, F>
[1464](https://docs.rs#1464)    where
[1465](https://docs.rs#1465)        Self: Sized,
[1466](https://docs.rs#1466)        F: FnMut(Self::Item, Self::Item) -> Result<Self::Item, (Self::Item, Self::Item)>,
[1467](https://docs.rs#1467)    {
[1468](https://docs.rs#1468)        adaptors::coalesce(self, f)
[1469](https://docs.rs#1469)    }

[1562](https://docs.rs#1562)    /// Return an iterator adaptor that produces elements that appear more than once during the
[1563](https://docs.rs#1563)    /// iteration. Duplicates are detected using hash and equality.
[1564](https://docs.rs#1564)    ///
[1565](https://docs.rs#1565)    /// The iterator is stable, returning the duplicate items in the order in which they occur in
[1566](https://docs.rs#1566)    /// the adapted iterator. Each duplicate item is returned exactly once. If an item appears more
[1567](https://docs.rs#1567)    /// than twice, the second item is the item retained and the rest are discarded.
[1568](https://docs.rs#1568)    ///
[1569](https://docs.rs#1569)    /// ```

[1572](https://docs.rs#1572)    /// let data = vec![10, 20, 30, 20, 40, 10, 50];
[1573](https://docs.rs#1573)    /// itertools::assert_equal(data.into_iter().duplicates(),
[1574](https://docs.rs#1574)    ///                         vec![20, 10]);
[1575](https://docs.rs#1575)    /// ```
[1576](https://docs.rs#1576)    #[cfg(feature = "use_std")]

[1580](https://docs.rs#1580)        Self::Item: Eq + Hash,
[1581](https://docs.rs#1581)    {
[1582](https://docs.rs#1582)        duplicates_impl::duplicates_with_hasher(self, RandomState::new())
[1583](https://docs.rs#1583)    }

[1585](https://docs.rs#1585)    /// Return an iterator which yields the same elements as the one returned by

[1594](https://docs.rs#1594)    /// use std::hash::RandomState;
[1595](https://docs.rs#1595)    /// use itertools::Itertools;
[1596](https://docs.rs#1596)    ///
[1597](https://docs.rs#1597)    /// let data = vec![10, 20, 30, 20, 40, 10, 50];
[1598](https://docs.rs#1598)    /// itertools::assert_equal(data.into_iter().duplicates_with_hasher(RandomState::new()),
[1599](https://docs.rs#1599)    ///                         vec![20,10]);
[1600](https://docs.rs#1600)    /// ```
[1601](https://docs.rs#1601)    #[cfg(feature = "use_std")]

[1607](https://docs.rs#1607)    {

[1622](https://docs.rs#1622)    /// use itertools::Itertools;
[1623](https://docs.rs#1623)    ///
[1624](https://docs.rs#1624)    /// let data = vec!["a", "bb", "aa", "c", "ccc"];
[1625](https://docs.rs#1625)    /// itertools::assert_equal(data.into_iter().duplicates_by(|s| s.len()),
[1626](https://docs.rs#1626)    ///                         vec!["aa", "c"]);
[1627](https://docs.rs#1627)    /// ```
[1628](https://docs.rs#1628)    #[cfg(feature = "use_std")]

[1797](https://docs.rs#1797)    /// Return an iterator adaptor that borrows from a `Clone`-able iterator

[1800](https://docs.rs#1800)    /// It uses the `Clone` trait to restore the original iterator so that the

[1804](https://docs.rs#1804)    /// ```
[1805](https://docs.rs#1805)    /// use itertools::Itertools;
[1806](https://docs.rs#1806)    ///
[1807](https://docs.rs#1807)    /// let mut hexadecimals = "0123456789abcdef".chars();
[1808](https://docs.rs#1808)    ///
[1809](https://docs.rs#1809)    /// let decimals = hexadecimals.take_while_ref(|c| c.is_numeric())
[1810](https://docs.rs#1810)    ///                            .collect::<String>();
[1811](https://docs.rs#1811)    /// assert_eq!(decimals, "0123456789");
[1812](https://docs.rs#1812)    /// assert_eq!(hexadecimals.next(), Some('a'));
[1813](https://docs.rs#1813)    /// ```
[1814](https://docs.rs#1814)    fn take_while_ref<F>(&mut self, accept: F) -> TakeWhileRef<'_, Self, F>
[1815](https://docs.rs#1815)    where
[1816](https://docs.rs#1816)        Self: Clone,
[1817](https://docs.rs#1817)        F: FnMut(&Self::Item) -> bool,
[1818](https://docs.rs#1818)    {
[1819](https://docs.rs#1819)        adaptors::take_while_ref(self, accept)
[1820](https://docs.rs#1820)    }

[1822](https://docs.rs#1822)    /// Returns an iterator adaptor that consumes elements while the given
[1823](https://docs.rs#1823)    /// predicate is `true`, *including* the element for which the predicate
[1824](https://docs.rs#1824)    /// first returned `false`.
[1825](https://docs.rs#1825)    ///
[1826](https://docs.rs#1826)    /// The [`.take_while()`][std::iter::Iterator::take_while] adaptor is useful
[1827](https://docs.rs#1827)    /// when you want items satisfying a predicate, but to know when to stop
[1828](https://docs.rs#1828)    /// taking elements, we have to consume that first element that doesn't
[1829](https://docs.rs#1829)    /// satisfy the predicate. This adaptor includes that element where
[1830](https://docs.rs#1830)    /// [`.take_while()`][std::iter::Iterator::take_while] would drop it.
[1831](https://docs.rs#1831)    ///
[1832](https://docs.rs#1832)    /// The [`.take_while_ref()`][crate::Itertools::take_while_ref] adaptor
[1833](https://docs.rs#1833)    /// serves a similar purpose, but this adaptor doesn't require [`Clone`]ing
[1834](https://docs.rs#1834)    /// the underlying elements.
[1835](https://docs.rs#1835)    ///
[1836](https://docs.rs#1836)    /// ```rust
[1837](https://docs.rs#1837)    /// # use itertools::Itertools;
[1838](https://docs.rs#1838)    /// let items = vec![1, 2, 3, 4, 5];
[1839](https://docs.rs#1839)    /// let filtered: Vec<_> = items
[1840](https://docs.rs#1840)    ///     .into_iter()
[1841](https://docs.rs#1841)    ///     .take_while_inclusive(|&n| n % 3 != 0)
[1842](https://docs.rs#1842)    ///     .collect();
[1843](https://docs.rs#1843)    ///
[1844](https://docs.rs#1844)    /// assert_eq!(filtered, vec![1, 2, 3]);
[1845](https://docs.rs#1845)    /// ```
[1846](https://docs.rs#1846)    ///
[1847](https://docs.rs#1847)    /// ```rust
[1848](https://docs.rs#1848)    /// # use itertools::Itertools;
[1849](https://docs.rs#1849)    /// let items = vec![1, 2, 3, 4, 5];
[1850](https://docs.rs#1850)    ///
[1851](https://docs.rs#1851)    /// let take_while_inclusive_result: Vec<_> = items
[1852](https://docs.rs#1852)    ///     .iter()
[1853](https://docs.rs#1853)    ///     .copied()
[1854](https://docs.rs#1854)    ///     .take_while_inclusive(|&n| n % 3 != 0)
[1855](https://docs.rs#1855)    ///     .collect();
[1856](https://docs.rs#1856)    /// let take_while_result: Vec<_> = items
[1857](https://docs.rs#1857)    ///     .into_iter()
[1858](https://docs.rs#1858)    ///     .take_while(|&n| n % 3 != 0)
[1859](https://docs.rs#1859)    ///     .collect();
[1860](https://docs.rs#1860)    ///
[1861](https://docs.rs#1861)    /// assert_eq!(take_while_inclusive_result, vec![1, 2, 3]);
[1862](https://docs.rs#1862)    /// assert_eq!(take_while_result, vec![1, 2]);
[1863](https://docs.rs#1863)    /// // both iterators have the same items remaining at this point---the 3
[1864](https://docs.rs#1864)    /// // is lost from the `take_while` vec
[1865](https://docs.rs#1865)    /// ```
[1866](https://docs.rs#1866)    ///
[1867](https://docs.rs#1867)    /// ```rust
[1868](https://docs.rs#1868)    /// # use itertools::Itertools;
[1869](https://docs.rs#1869)    /// #[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
[1870](https://docs.rs#1870)    /// struct NoCloneImpl(i32);
[1871](https://docs.rs#1871)    ///
[1872](https://docs.rs#1872)    /// let non_cloneable_items: Vec<_> = vec![1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
[1873](https://docs.rs#1873)    ///     .into_iter()
[1874](https://docs.rs#1874)    ///     .map(NoCloneImpl)
[1875](https://docs.rs#1875)    ///     .collect();
[1876](https://docs.rs#1876)    /// let filtered: Vec<_> = non_cloneable_items
[1877](https://docs.rs#1877)    ///     .into_iter()
[1878](https://docs.rs#1878)    ///     .take_while_inclusive(|n| n.0 % 3 != 0)
[1879](https://docs.rs#1879)    ///     .collect();
[1880](https://docs.rs#1880)    /// let expected: Vec<_> = vec![1, 2, 3].into_iter().map(NoCloneImpl).collect();
[1881](https://docs.rs#1881)    /// assert_eq!(filtered, expected);
[1882](https://docs.rs#1882)    #[doc(alias = "take_until")]
[1883](https://docs.rs#1883)    fn take_while_inclusive<F>(self, accept: F) -> TakeWhileInclusive<Self, F>
[1884](https://docs.rs#1884)    where
[1885](https://docs.rs#1885)        Self: Sized,
[1886](https://docs.rs#1886)        F: FnMut(&Self::Item) -> bool,
[1887](https://docs.rs#1887)    {
[1888](https://docs.rs#1888)        take_while_inclusive::TakeWhileInclusive::new(self, accept)
[1889](https://docs.rs#1889)    }

[1912](https://docs.rs#1912)    /// Return an iterator adaptor that iterates over the combinations of the
[1913](https://docs.rs#1913)    /// elements from an iterator.
[1914](https://docs.rs#1914)    ///
[1915](https://docs.rs#1915)    /// Iterator element can be any homogeneous tuple of type `Self::Item` with
[1916](https://docs.rs#1916)    /// size up to 12.
[1917](https://docs.rs#1917)    ///
[1918](https://docs.rs#1918)    /// # Guarantees
[1919](https://docs.rs#1919)    ///
[1920](https://docs.rs#1920)    /// If the adapted iterator is deterministic,
[1921](https://docs.rs#1921)    /// this iterator adapter yields items in a reliable order.
[1922](https://docs.rs#1922)    ///
[1923](https://docs.rs#1923)    /// ```
[1924](https://docs.rs#1924)    /// use itertools::Itertools;
[1925](https://docs.rs#1925)    ///
[1926](https://docs.rs#1926)    /// let mut v = Vec::new();
[1927](https://docs.rs#1927)    /// for (a, b) in (1..5).tuple_combinations() {
[1928](https://docs.rs#1928)    ///     v.push((a, b));
[1929](https://docs.rs#1929)    /// }
[1930](https://docs.rs#1930)    /// assert_eq!(v, vec![(1, 2), (1, 3), (1, 4), (2, 3), (2, 4), (3, 4)]);
[1931](https://docs.rs#1931)    ///
[1932](https://docs.rs#1932)    /// let mut it = (1..5).tuple_combinations();
[1933](https://docs.rs#1933)    /// assert_eq!(Some((1, 2, 3)), it.next());
[1934](https://docs.rs#1934)    /// assert_eq!(Some((1, 2, 4)), it.next());
[1935](https://docs.rs#1935)    /// assert_eq!(Some((1, 3, 4)), it.next());
[1936](https://docs.rs#1936)    /// assert_eq!(Some((2, 3, 4)), it.next());
[1937](https://docs.rs#1937)    /// assert_eq!(None, it.next());
[1938](https://docs.rs#1938)    ///
[1939](https://docs.rs#1939)    /// // this requires a type hint
[1940](https://docs.rs#1940)    /// let it = (1..5).tuple_combinations::<(_, _, _)>();
[1941](https://docs.rs#1941)    /// itertools::assert_equal(it, vec![(1, 2, 3), (1, 2, 4), (1, 3, 4), (2, 3, 4)]);
[1942](https://docs.rs#1942)    ///
[1943](https://docs.rs#1943)    /// // you can also specify the complete type
[1944](https://docs.rs#1944)    /// use itertools::TupleCombinations;
[1945](https://docs.rs#1945)    /// use std::ops::Range;
[1946](https://docs.rs#1946)    ///
[1947](https://docs.rs#1947)    /// let it: TupleCombinations<Range<u32>, (u32, u32, u32)> = (1..5).tuple_combinations();
[1948](https://docs.rs#1948)    /// itertools::assert_equal(it, vec![(1, 2, 3), (1, 2, 4), (1, 3, 4), (2, 3, 4)]);
[1949](https://docs.rs#1949)    /// ```
[1950](https://docs.rs#1950)    #[deprecated(note = "Use .array_combinations() instead", since = "0.15.0")]
[1951](https://docs.rs#1951)    fn tuple_combinations<T>(self) -> TupleCombinations<Self, T>
[1952](https://docs.rs#1952)    where
[1953](https://docs.rs#1953)        Self: Sized,
[1954](https://docs.rs#1954)        Self::Item: Clone,
[1955](https://docs.rs#1955)        T: adaptors::HasCombination<Self>,
[1956](https://docs.rs#1956)    {
[1957](https://docs.rs#1957)        adaptors::tuple_combinations(self)
[1958](https://docs.rs#1958)    }

[2106](https://docs.rs#2106)    /// Return an iterator adaptor that iterates over all k-permutations of the
[2107](https://docs.rs#2107)    /// elements from an iterator.
[2108](https://docs.rs#2108)    ///
[2109](https://docs.rs#2109)    /// Iterator element type is `Vec<Self::Item>` with length `k`. The iterator
[2110](https://docs.rs#2110)    /// produces a new `Vec` per iteration, and clones the iterator elements.
[2111](https://docs.rs#2111)    ///
[2112](https://docs.rs#2112)    /// If `k` is greater than the length of the input iterator, the resultant
[2113](https://docs.rs#2113)    /// iterator adaptor will be empty.
[2114](https://docs.rs#2114)    ///
[2115](https://docs.rs#2115)    /// If you are looking for permutations with replacements,
[2116](https://docs.rs#2116)    /// use `repeat_n(iter, k).multi_cartesian_product()` instead.
[2117](https://docs.rs#2117)    ///
[2118](https://docs.rs#2118)    /// ```
[2119](https://docs.rs#2119)    /// use itertools::Itertools;
[2120](https://docs.rs#2120)    ///
[2121](https://docs.rs#2121)    /// let perms = (5..8).permutations(2);
[2122](https://docs.rs#2122)    /// itertools::assert_equal(perms, vec![
[2123](https://docs.rs#2123)    ///     vec![5, 6],
[2124](https://docs.rs#2124)    ///     vec![5, 7],
[2125](https://docs.rs#2125)    ///     vec![6, 5],
[2126](https://docs.rs#2126)    ///     vec![6, 7],
[2127](https://docs.rs#2127)    ///     vec![7, 5],
[2128](https://docs.rs#2128)    ///     vec![7, 6],
[2129](https://docs.rs#2129)    /// ]);
[2130](https://docs.rs#2130)    /// ```
[2131](https://docs.rs#2131)    ///
[2132](https://docs.rs#2132)    /// Note: Permutations does not take into account the equality of the iterated values.
[2133](https://docs.rs#2133)    ///
[2134](https://docs.rs#2134)    /// ```
[2135](https://docs.rs#2135)    /// use itertools::Itertools;
[2136](https://docs.rs#2136)    ///
[2137](https://docs.rs#2137)    /// let it = vec![2, 2].into_iter().permutations(2);
[2138](https://docs.rs#2138)    /// itertools::assert_equal(it, vec![
[2139](https://docs.rs#2139)    ///     vec![2, 2], // Note: these are the same
[2140](https://docs.rs#2140)    ///     vec![2, 2], // Note: these are the same
[2141](https://docs.rs#2141)    /// ]);
[2142](https://docs.rs#2142)    /// ```
[2143](https://docs.rs#2143)    ///
[2144](https://docs.rs#2144)    /// Note: The source iterator is collected lazily, and will not be
[2145](https://docs.rs#2145)    /// re-iterated if the permutations adaptor is completed and re-iterated.
[2146](https://docs.rs#2146)    #[cfg(feature = "use_alloc")]
[2147](https://docs.rs#2147)    fn permutations(self, k: usize) -> Permutations<Self>
[2148](https://docs.rs#2148)    where
[2149](https://docs.rs#2149)        Self: Sized,
[2150](https://docs.rs#2150)        Self::Item: Clone,
[2151](https://docs.rs#2151)    {
[2152](https://docs.rs#2152)        permutations::permutations(self, k)
[2153](https://docs.rs#2153)    }

[2160](https://docs.rs#2160)    ///
[2161](https://docs.rs#2161)    /// The powerset of a set contains all subsets including the empty set and the full

[2168](https://docs.rs#2168)    /// ```
[2169](https://docs.rs#2169)    /// use itertools::Itertools;
[2170](https://docs.rs#2170)    ///
[2171](https://docs.rs#2171)    /// let sets = (1..4).powerset().collect::<Vec<_>>();
[2172](https://docs.rs#2172)    /// itertools::assert_equal(sets, vec![
[2173](https://docs.rs#2173)    ///     vec![],
[2174](https://docs.rs#2174)    ///     vec![1],
[2175](https://docs.rs#2175)    ///     vec![2],
[2176](https://docs.rs#2176)    ///     vec![3],
[2177](https://docs.rs#2177)    ///     vec![1, 2],
[2178](https://docs.rs#2178)    ///     vec![1, 3],
[2179](https://docs.rs#2179)    ///     vec![2, 3],
[2180](https://docs.rs#2180)    ///     vec![1, 2, 3],
[2181](https://docs.rs#2181)    /// ]);
[2182](https://docs.rs#2182)    /// ```
[2183](https://docs.rs#2183)    #[cfg(feature = "use_alloc")]
[2184](https://docs.rs#2184)    fn powerset(self) -> Powerset<Self>

[2186](https://docs.rs#2186)        Self: Sized,
[2187](https://docs.rs#2187)        Self::Item: Clone,
[2188](https://docs.rs#2188)    {
[2189](https://docs.rs#2189)        powerset::powerset(self)
[2190](https://docs.rs#2190)    }

[2403](https://docs.rs#2403)    /// Find the value of the first element satisfying a predicate or return the last element, if any.

[2418](https://docs.rs#2418)    ///

[2420](https://docs.rs#2420)    /// assert_eq!(input.into_iter().find_or_last(Result::is_ok), Some(Err(22)));
[2421](https://docs.rs#2421)    ///
[2422](https://docs.rs#2422)    /// assert_eq!(std::iter::empty::<Result<(), i32>>().find_or_last(Result::is_ok), None);
[2423](https://docs.rs#2423)    /// ```
[2424](https://docs.rs#2424)    fn find_or_last<P>(mut self, mut predicate: P) -> Option<Self::Item>
[2425](https://docs.rs#2425)    where
[2426](https://docs.rs#2426)        Self: Sized,
[2427](https://docs.rs#2427)        P: FnMut(&Self::Item) -> bool,
[2428](https://docs.rs#2428)    {
[2429](https://docs.rs#2429)        let mut prev = None;
[2430](https://docs.rs#2430)        self.find_map(|x| {
[2431](https://docs.rs#2431)            if predicate(&x) {
[2432](https://docs.rs#2432)                Some(x)
[2433](https://docs.rs#2433)            } else {
[2434](https://docs.rs#2434)                prev = Some(x);
[2435](https://docs.rs#2435)                None
[2436](https://docs.rs#2436)            }
[2437](https://docs.rs#2437)        })
[2438](https://docs.rs#2438)        .or(prev)
[2439](https://docs.rs#2439)    }
[2440](https://docs.rs#2440)    /// Find the value of the first element satisfying a predicate or return the first element, if any.
[2441](https://docs.rs#2441)    ///
[2442](https://docs.rs#2442)    /// The iterator is not advanced past the first element found.
[2443](https://docs.rs#2443)    ///
[2444](https://docs.rs#2444)    /// ```
[2445](https://docs.rs#2445)    /// use itertools::Itertools;
[2446](https://docs.rs#2446)    ///
[2447](https://docs.rs#2447)    /// let numbers = [1, 2, 3, 4];
[2448](https://docs.rs#2448)    /// assert_eq!(numbers.iter().find_or_first(|&&x| x > 5), Some(&1));
[2449](https://docs.rs#2449)    /// assert_eq!(numbers.iter().find_or_first(|&&x| x > 2), Some(&3));
[2450](https://docs.rs#2450)    /// assert_eq!(std::iter::empty::<i32>().find_or_first(|&x| x > 5), None);
[2451](https://docs.rs#2451)    ///
[2452](https://docs.rs#2452)    /// // An iterator of Results can return the first Ok or the first Err:
[2453](https://docs.rs#2453)    /// let input = vec![Err(()), Ok(11), Err(()), Ok(22)];
[2454](https://docs.rs#2454)    /// assert_eq!(input.into_iter().find_or_first(Result::is_ok), Some(Ok(11)));
[2455](https://docs.rs#2455)    ///
[2456](https://docs.rs#2456)    /// let input: Vec<Result<(), i32>> = vec![Err(11), Err(22)];
[2457](https://docs.rs#2457)    /// assert_eq!(input.into_iter().find_or_first(Result::is_ok), Some(Err(11)));
[2458](https://docs.rs#2458)    ///
[2459](https://docs.rs#2459)    /// assert_eq!(std::iter::empty::<Result<(), i32>>().find_or_first(Result::is_ok), None);
[2460](https://docs.rs#2460)    /// ```
[2461](https://docs.rs#2461)    fn find_or_first<P>(mut self, mut predicate: P) -> Option<Self::Item>
[2462](https://docs.rs#2462)    where
[2463](https://docs.rs#2463)        Self: Sized,
[2464](https://docs.rs#2464)        P: FnMut(&Self::Item) -> bool,
[2465](https://docs.rs#2465)    {
[2466](https://docs.rs#2466)        let first = self.next()?;
[2467](https://docs.rs#2467)        Some(if predicate(&first) {
[2468](https://docs.rs#2468)            first
[2469](https://docs.rs#2469)        } else {
[2470](https://docs.rs#2470)            self.find(|x| predicate(x)).unwrap_or(first)
[2471](https://docs.rs#2471)        })
[2472](https://docs.rs#2472)    }
[2473](https://docs.rs#2473)    /// Returns `true` if the given item is present in this iterator.
[2474](https://docs.rs#2474)    ///
[2475](https://docs.rs#2475)    /// This method is short-circuiting. If the given item is present in this
[2476](https://docs.rs#2476)    /// iterator, this method will consume the iterator up-to-and-including
[2477](https://docs.rs#2477)    /// the item. If the given item is not present in this iterator, the
[2478](https://docs.rs#2478)    /// iterator will be exhausted.
[2479](https://docs.rs#2479)    ///
[2480](https://docs.rs#2480)    /// ```
[2481](https://docs.rs#2481)    /// use itertools::Itertools;
[2482](https://docs.rs#2482)    ///
[2483](https://docs.rs#2483)    /// #[derive(PartialEq, Debug)]
[2484](https://docs.rs#2484)    /// enum Enum { A, B, C, D, E, }
[2485](https://docs.rs#2485)    ///
[2486](https://docs.rs#2486)    /// let mut iter = vec![Enum::A, Enum::B, Enum::C, Enum::D].into_iter();
[2487](https://docs.rs#2487)    ///
[2488](https://docs.rs#2488)    /// // search `iter` for `B`
[2489](https://docs.rs#2489)    /// assert_eq!(iter.contains(&Enum::B), true);
[2490](https://docs.rs#2490)    /// // `B` was found, so the iterator now rests at the item after `B` (i.e, `C`).
[2491](https://docs.rs#2491)    /// assert_eq!(iter.next(), Some(Enum::C));
[2492](https://docs.rs#2492)    ///
[2493](https://docs.rs#2493)    /// // search `iter` for `E`
[2494](https://docs.rs#2494)    /// assert_eq!(iter.contains(&Enum::E), false);
[2495](https://docs.rs#2495)    /// // `E` wasn't found, so `iter` is now exhausted
[2496](https://docs.rs#2496)    /// assert_eq!(iter.next(), None);
[2497](https://docs.rs#2497)    /// ```
[2498](https://docs.rs#2498)    fn contains<Q>(&mut self, query: &Q) -> bool
[2499](https://docs.rs#2499)    where
[2500](https://docs.rs#2500)        Self: Sized,
[2501](https://docs.rs#2501)        Self::Item: Borrow<Q>,
[2502](https://docs.rs#2502)        Q: PartialEq + ?Sized,
[2503](https://docs.rs#2503)    {
[2504](https://docs.rs#2504)        self.any(|x| x.borrow() == query)
[2505](https://docs.rs#2505)    }
[2506](https://docs.rs#2506)
[2507](https://docs.rs#2507)    /// Check whether all elements compare equal.
[2508](https://docs.rs#2508)    ///
[2509](https://docs.rs#2509)    /// Empty iterators are considered to have equal elements:
[2510](https://docs.rs#2510)    ///
[2511](https://docs.rs#2511)    /// ```
[2512](https://docs.rs#2512)    /// use itertools::Itertools;
[2513](https://docs.rs#2513)    ///
[2514](https://docs.rs#2514)    /// let data = vec![1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3, 4, 5, 5];
[2515](https://docs.rs#2515)    /// assert!(!data.iter().all_equal());
[2516](https://docs.rs#2516)    /// assert!(data[0..3].iter().all_equal());
[2517](https://docs.rs#2517)    /// assert!(data[3..5].iter().all_equal());
[2518](https://docs.rs#2518)    /// assert!(data[5..8].iter().all_equal());
[2519](https://docs.rs#2519)    ///
[2520](https://docs.rs#2520)    /// let data: Option<usize> = None;
[2521](https://docs.rs#2521)    /// assert!(data.into_iter().all_equal());
[2522](https://docs.rs#2522)    /// ```
[2523](https://docs.rs#2523)    fn all_equal(&mut self) -> bool
[2524](https://docs.rs#2524)    where
[2525](https://docs.rs#2525)        Self: Sized,
[2526](https://docs.rs#2526)        Self::Item: PartialEq,
[2527](https://docs.rs#2527)    {
[2528](https://docs.rs#2528)        match self.next() {
[2529](https://docs.rs#2529)            None => true,
[2530](https://docs.rs#2530)            Some(a) => self.all(|x| a == x),
[2531](https://docs.rs#2531)        }
[2532](https://docs.rs#2532)    }
[2533](https://docs.rs#2533)
[2534](https://docs.rs#2534)    /// If there are elements and they are all equal, return a single copy of that element.
[2535](https://docs.rs#2535)    /// If there are no elements, return an Error containing None.
[2536](https://docs.rs#2536)    /// If there are elements and they are not all equal, return a tuple containing the first
[2537](https://docs.rs#2537)    /// two non-equal elements found.
[2538](https://docs.rs#2538)    ///
[2539](https://docs.rs#2539)    /// ```
[2540](https://docs.rs#2540)    /// use itertools::{Itertools, AllEqualValueError};
[2541](https://docs.rs#2541)    ///
[2542](https://docs.rs#2542)    /// let data = vec![1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3, 4, 5, 5];
[2543](https://docs.rs#2543)    /// assert_eq!(data.iter().all_equal_value(), Err(AllEqualValueError(Some([&1, &2]))));
[2544](https://docs.rs#2544)    /// assert_eq!(data[0..3].iter().all_equal_value(), Ok(&1));
[2545](https://docs.rs#2545)    /// assert_eq!(data[3..5].iter().all_equal_value(), Ok(&2));
[2546](https://docs.rs#2546)    /// assert_eq!(data[5..8].iter().all_equal_value(), Ok(&3));
[2547](https://docs.rs#2547)    ///
[2548](https://docs.rs#2548)    /// let data: Option<usize> = None;
[2549](https://docs.rs#2549)    /// assert_eq!(data.into_iter().all_equal_value(), Err(AllEqualValueError(None)));
[2550](https://docs.rs#2550)    /// ```
[2551](https://docs.rs#2551)    #[allow(clippy::type_complexity)]
[2552](https://docs.rs#2552)    fn all_equal_value(&mut self) -> Result<Self::Item, AllEqualValueError<Self::Item>>
[2553](https://docs.rs#2553)    where
[2554](https://docs.rs#2554)        Self: Sized,
[2555](https://docs.rs#2555)        Self::Item: PartialEq,
[2556](https://docs.rs#2556)    {
[2557](https://docs.rs#2557)        let first = self.next().ok_or(AllEqualValueError(None))?;
[2558](https://docs.rs#2558)        let other = self.find(|x| x != &first);
[2559](https://docs.rs#2559)        if let Some(other) = other {
[2560](https://docs.rs#2560)            Err(AllEqualValueError(Some([first, other])))
[2561](https://docs.rs#2561)        } else {
[2562](https://docs.rs#2562)            Ok(first)
[2563](https://docs.rs#2563)        }
[2564](https://docs.rs#2564)    }

[2590](https://docs.rs#2590)    /// Check whether all elements are unique (non equal). The specified hash builder is used for

[2616](https://docs.rs#2616)    /// Consume the first `n` elements from the iterator eagerly,
[2617](https://docs.rs#2617)    /// and return the same iterator again.
[2618](https://docs.rs#2618)    ///
[2619](https://docs.rs#2619)    /// It works similarly to `.skip(n)` except it is eager and
[2620](https://docs.rs#2620)    /// preserves the iterator type.
[2621](https://docs.rs#2621)    ///
[2622](https://docs.rs#2622)    /// ```
[2623](https://docs.rs#2623)    /// use itertools::Itertools;
[2624](https://docs.rs#2624)    ///
[2625](https://docs.rs#2625)    /// let iter = "αβγ".chars().dropping(2);
[2626](https://docs.rs#2626)    /// itertools::assert_equal(iter, "γ".chars());
[2627](https://docs.rs#2627)    /// ```
[2628](https://docs.rs#2628)    ///
[2629](https://docs.rs#2629)    /// *Fusing notes: if the iterator is exhausted by dropping,
[2630](https://docs.rs#2630)    /// the result of calling `.next()` again depends on the iterator implementation.*
[2631](https://docs.rs#2631)    fn dropping(mut self, n: usize) -> Self
[2632](https://docs.rs#2632)    where
[2633](https://docs.rs#2633)        Self: Sized,
[2634](https://docs.rs#2634)    {
[2635](https://docs.rs#2635)        if n > 0 {
[2636](https://docs.rs#2636)            self.nth(n - 1);
[2637](https://docs.rs#2637)        }
[2638](https://docs.rs#2638)        self
[2639](https://docs.rs#2639)    }
[2640](https://docs.rs#2640)
[2641](https://docs.rs#2641)    /// Consume the last `n` elements from the iterator eagerly,
[2642](https://docs.rs#2642)    /// and return the same iterator again.
[2643](https://docs.rs#2643)    ///
[2644](https://docs.rs#2644)    /// This is only possible on double ended iterators. `n` may be
[2645](https://docs.rs#2645)    /// larger than the number of elements.
[2646](https://docs.rs#2646)    ///
[2647](https://docs.rs#2647)    /// Note: This method is eager, dropping the back elements immediately and
[2648](https://docs.rs#2648)    /// preserves the iterator type.
[2649](https://docs.rs#2649)    ///
[2650](https://docs.rs#2650)    /// ```
[2651](https://docs.rs#2651)    /// use itertools::Itertools;
[2652](https://docs.rs#2652)    ///
[2653](https://docs.rs#2653)    /// let init = vec![0, 3, 6, 9].into_iter().dropping_back(1);
[2654](https://docs.rs#2654)    /// itertools::assert_equal(init, vec![0, 3, 6]);
[2655](https://docs.rs#2655)    /// ```
[2656](https://docs.rs#2656)    fn dropping_back(mut self, n: usize) -> Self

[2658](https://docs.rs#2658)        Self: Sized + DoubleEndedIterator,
[2659](https://docs.rs#2659)    {
[2660](https://docs.rs#2660)        if n > 0 {
[2661](https://docs.rs#2661)            (&mut self).rev().nth(n - 1);
[2662](https://docs.rs#2662)        }
[2663](https://docs.rs#2663)        self
[2664](https://docs.rs#2664)    }

[2749](https://docs.rs#2749)        J: IntoIterator<Item = A>,

[2757](https://docs.rs#2757)    /// Combine all iterator elements into one `String`, separated by `sep`.
[2758](https://docs.rs#2758)    ///
[2759](https://docs.rs#2759)    /// Use the `Display` implementation of each element.
[2760](https://docs.rs#2760)    ///
[2761](https://docs.rs#2761)    /// ```
[2762](https://docs.rs#2762)    /// use itertools::Itertools;
[2763](https://docs.rs#2763)    ///
[2764](https://docs.rs#2764)    /// assert_eq!(["a", "b", "c"].iter().join(", "), "a, b, c");
[2765](https://docs.rs#2765)    /// assert_eq!([1, 2, 3].iter().join(", "), "1, 2, 3");
[2766](https://docs.rs#2766)    /// ```
[2767](https://docs.rs#2767)    #[cfg(feature = "use_alloc")]
[2768](https://docs.rs#2768)    fn join(&mut self, sep: &str) -> String
[2769](https://docs.rs#2769)    where
[2770](https://docs.rs#2770)        Self::Item: std::fmt::Display,
[2771](https://docs.rs#2771)    {
[2772](https://docs.rs#2772)        match self.next() {
[2773](https://docs.rs#2773)            None => String::new(),
[2774](https://docs.rs#2774)            Some(first_elt) => {
[2775](https://docs.rs#2775)                // estimate lower bound of capacity needed
[2776](https://docs.rs#2776)                let (lower, _) = self.size_hint();
[2777](https://docs.rs#2777)                let mut result = String::with_capacity(sep.len() * lower);
[2778](https://docs.rs#2778)                write!(&mut result, "{first_elt}").unwrap();
[2779](https://docs.rs#2779)                self.for_each(|elt| {
[2780](https://docs.rs#2780)                    result.push_str(sep);
[2781](https://docs.rs#2781)                    write!(&mut result, "{elt}").unwrap();
[2782](https://docs.rs#2782)                });
[2783](https://docs.rs#2783)                result
[2784](https://docs.rs#2784)            }
[2785](https://docs.rs#2785)        }
[2786](https://docs.rs#2786)    }

[2788](https://docs.rs#2788)    /// Format all iterator elements, separated by `sep`.
[2789](https://docs.rs#2789)    ///
[2790](https://docs.rs#2790)    /// All elements are formatted (any formatting trait)
[2791](https://docs.rs#2791)    /// with `sep` inserted between each element.

[2798](https://docs.rs#2798)    /// let data = [1.1, 2.71828, -3.];

[2800](https://docs.rs#2800)    ///     format!("{:.2}", data.iter().format(", ")),
[2801](https://docs.rs#2801)    ///            "1.10, 2.72, -3.00");
[2802](https://docs.rs#2802)    /// ```
[2803](https://docs.rs#2803)    fn format(self, sep: &str) -> Format<'_, Self>

[2805](https://docs.rs#2805)        Self: Sized,
[2806](https://docs.rs#2806)    {
[2807](https://docs.rs#2807)        format::new_format_default(self, sep)
